# Gems

_Generated from PoB tree data `3.29`. Regenerate after any data update - this script
rebuilds `gems.db` too._

A gem may be used IF AND ONLY IF it has a row in `data/gems.db` - the 36 legacy gems
are excluded at generation. Memory-sourced names are hypotheses - one query settles
existence and legality together; zero rows, for any reason, means no. Nothing in
PoB's UI or file format stops you picking an unobtainable gem - check while choosing;
`validate.lua` catches it after the fact, when it costs a rebuild.

## Querying gems.db

Run `sqlite3` with paths from the repo root (from `src/`, prefix `../`). Names use
PoB's convention: supports carry no "Support" suffix (`Melee Physical Damage`). For
a gem's full behaviour beyond the columns, grep its entry in
`src/Data/Skills/act_*.lua` / `sup_*.lua`.

- `gems(id, name, variant_id, kind, vaal, color, max_level, req_level, cast_time,
  crit_chance, dmg_effectiveness, cost, cost_multiplier, tag_string, description,
  upgrade_of, upgraded_version)` - kind `active|support`; color `R|G|B|W`;
  `variant_id` is the skillId build XMLs reference. Numeric stats are snapshots at
  `max_level`: `req_level` = character level needed there, `cost` like `Mana=25` /
  `Soul=30`, `cost_multiplier` is the support's total % (130 = 30% more, NULL = no
  multiplier - reservation-style supports). NULL `crit_chance`/`dmg_effectiveness`
  on actives = field does not apply (attacks use weapon crit; DoTs have no
  effectiveness).
- `gem_tags(gem_id, tag)` - lowercase game tags, one per row; AND tags by joining
  `gem_tags` once per required tag.
- `meta(key, value)` - `tree_version`, `generated_at`.

Canonical queries:

```sh
DB=.claude/skills/cook/data/gems.db
# existence - zero rows means DO NOT USE, whatever the reason
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT id, kind, max_level FROM gems WHERE name='Frostmage';"
# mana-tight builds: supports at low cost multiplier
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT name, cost_multiplier FROM gems WHERE kind='support'
  AND cost_multiplier <= 110;"
# tag AND: triggerable spells
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT g.name FROM gems g
  JOIN gem_tags t1 ON t1.gem_id=g.id AND t1.tag='spell'
  JOIN gem_tags t2 ON t2.gem_id=g.id AND t2.tag='trigger' WHERE g.kind='active';"
```

## Upgraded support tiers

`grantedEffect.plusVersionOf` links a support to its upgraded version - in the db,
`upgraded_version` (and `upgrade_of` as the reverse link). 20 supports have an
obtainable upgrade; NULL `upgraded_version` means none exists, so do not go looking
for one. Most upgrades are a renamed gem rather than an `Awakened *` one - that
line is gone bar Empower, Enhance and Enlighten. An upgrade beats its base at every
level, so prefer it whenever it exists.

```sh
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT name, upgraded_version FROM gems WHERE upgraded_version IS NOT NULL;"
```

## Level caps

Every gem can be corrupted to one level above its natural max, with no exceptions.
Cap is always `naturalMaxLevel + 1`; per-gem natural maxes are the `max_level` column.
